why_delta_target: the prior absolute-value model (test MAE 5.69) showed a same-direction, different-magnitude bias across two real backtests (8.29 vs 3.66 degC) -- the signature of a model implicitly encoding 'what regime was I trained in' via absolute temperature level. Predicting the CHANGE, with the target's own lag/rolling-mean/EMA expressed as deviation-from-now (momentum) instead of absolute level, removes that leak -- the same fix already proven in feature/digital-twin-ml (a colleague's branch), which found absolute-target models scored worse than persistence.

live_deployment_backtest.how: python -m etl.backtest_forecast -- runs backend.forecast.forecast_from_recent() (the exact function the live API calls) against real historical 1-second data, scored against a causally-denoised actual.
live_deployment_backtest.conclusion: the delta-target retrain closes the training/serving gap almost completely (2.53 training vs ~2.30 combined empirical), AND removes the regime-dependent bias swing seen on the prior absolute-value model (both windows now near-zero bias, both comfortably under the 5 degC target). This is the strongest verified result in this project's history for this task.
